article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab is advancing towards the Andhra Pradesh coast as the Centre places four states and Puducherry on alert.
The system may intensify significantly before its projected October 28 landfall near Yanam.

The Centre on Monday sounded an alert in four states and Puducherry and stepped up preparedness as Cyclone Arnab intensified over the Bay of Bengal and moved towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, where it is expected to make landfall on the morning of October 28.
Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry have been placed on alert.
In its morning bulletin on Monday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the cyclonic storm was centred over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal at 5:30 am.
It was located around 650 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and was moving westwards at a speed of 15 kmph.
The storm is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by midnight on Monday and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm on Tuesday.
According to the IMD, Arnab is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by the forenoon of October 28.
It is likely to bring sustained wind speeds of 115–125 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 140 kmph.
Amid the approaching storm, Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan chaired a meeting of the National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) to assess preparedness and coordinate relief measures.
Authorities in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have also been asked to remain vigilant in view of the forecast of heavy rainfall.
National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams have been deployed, with additional personnel kept on standby.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: APEPDCL opens 41 control rooms, keeps 4,056 workers ready to restore power

article_sentences: The Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) has stepped up its preparedness for Cyclone Arnab and is concentrating on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Godavari and Kakinada districts, towards which the storm is expected to make landfall.

Following the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s warning about Cyclone Arnab over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal, the utility has mobilised personnel, machinery and electrical materials to minimise disruptions and speed up power restoration in affected areas.
APEPDCL has opened 30 divisional control rooms, in addition to 11 circle-level control rooms, to monitor the situation and coordinate emergency response.
Kakinada and East Godavari have three divisional control rooms each, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema has two.
A separate cell has been established at the corporate office to coordinate manpower deployment round the clock under the supervision of the Chief General Manager (Operations and Customer Service).
APEPDCL CMD I. Prudhvi Tej held a teleconference with senior engineering officials to review cyclone preparedness.
The utility has also sought 150 teams of 10 personnel each from the Southern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APSPDCL) and requested additional materials from it.
The utility has arranged 394 contractor teams comprising 4,056 personnel for emergency response and restoration work.
The available resources include 211 diesel generator sets, 273 pole-drilling machines, 517 power saws and 318 earth movers and cranes.
A fleet of 366 departmental and private vehicles has been listed to transport personnel and materials to affected locations.
Another 100 mobile handsets have been arranged for communication during emergency operations.
APEPDCL said it had stocks of conductors, cables, distribution transformers and electric poles as of October 25.

article_sentences: The story so far: The Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission issued a notification on October 19, 2026, for elections to the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs), scheduled for November 3.

The decision to hold the elections in the Kotia group of villages, whose jurisdiction has been disputed by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha since Independence, triggered protests across the political spectrum in Odisha.
The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), Congress, and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Andhra Pradesh of undermining Odisha’s territorial integrity.

The Odisha government said on October 23, 2026, that it had filed a contempt of court petition against the Andhra Pradesh government in the Supreme Court challenging the notification for the forthcoming election in Kotia.
Why Kotia is disputed?
As many as 21 villages in the Kotia group, under Pottangi Tahasil of Odisha’s Koraput district, have been at the centre of a territorial dispute with Andhra Pradesh since 1955.
According to an Odisha government brief on the dispute, Odisha exercised administrative control over these villages from 1936.
The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages.
Odisha protested through its Chief Secretary, but Andhra Pradesh countered that it had been collecting revenue there since 1947 and that residents had participated in the State’s 1954 elections.
In 1959, Andhra Pradesh cited a 1942 boundary demarcation by M. Gilby, Assistant Director of Survey, Madras Province, claiming it had been carried out with Odisha’s consent.
Odisha rejected the claim, arguing that Gilby had wrongly assumed his demarcation conformed to the Government of India (Constitution of Orissa) Order, 1936.
Both States held general elections in the disputed area in 1967.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to examine a petition challenging the special intensive revision (SIR) of Maharashtra’s electoral rolls, following concerns that voters temporarily displaced by redevelopment projects had been excluded.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the Centre, the Election Commission of India and other respondents.
The matter will be heard next on 5 November.
The petition was filed by Arun Anandagiri, a chartered accountant and journalist.
Appearing for him, senior advocate.

Arvind Datar told the court that voters who had temporarily moved out of their homes during redevelopment in Mumbai and Pune were being categorised as “person not found” and removed from the draft rolls.
Datar submitted that around two crore of Maharashtra’s nearly 9.79 crore voters had been excluded.
He also claimed that another 1.22 crore electors had been struck off under the category of “logical discrepancies”.
The petition seeks to keep the revision exercise in abeyance until the court decides the challenge.
It also asks that no voter included in the pre-SIR electoral rolls be excluded or deleted during this period.

According to figures released by the state chief electoral officer’s office, 2,06,88,487 electors — 21.14 per cent of the state’s 9,78,54,049 registered voters — were excluded from the draft rolls because they could not be traced at their recorded addresses during the exercise.
The challenge places the treatment of temporarily relocated residents under judicial scrutiny, particularly those who have moved while their homes undergo redevelopment.

stories.summary: Islamabad, Oct 26: Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir, Saudi Arabia's defence minister and Turkish intelligence chief are expected to jointly meet top Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss the regional security situation, according to officials. In separate statements, Pakistan, Saudi and Iranian authorities confirmed the meeting, amid fears that escalating tensions in the region could draw more countries into the fighting. The meeting also comes amid raging tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in recent weeks, with the Iran-backed group claiming attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and military sites. Saudi Arabia has reported intercepting missiles and drones targeting the kingdom. Field Marshal Munir is visiting Tehran on an "official visit," the Pakistan Army said in a brief statement, without giving details of the trip. This is his second trip to Tehran within a week, amid indications that the US might be preparing for another round of fighting with Iran. Hours earlier, the Iranian Supreme National Security Council's Deputy Secretary Ali Bagheri said that "senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkiye will travel to Tehran as part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia,” according to the state-run IRNA news agency. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye are part of the Makkah Joint Defence agreement signed in August. According to the pact, any attack on one of the three countries would be treated as an attack against all. The high-level meeting comes days after the Pakistan Army chief met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei in Tehran. Bagheri told state TV that among the visiting dignitaries would be Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and Pakistan's Army chief Munir. "The purpose of these senior officials’ trip is consultation with Major General Mohsen Rezaei regarding regional security," he said. "All three countries attending this meeting, along with Iran, can take an effective step toward creating endogenous security within the framework of Iran's effective idea for regional security-building with the participation of regional actors, drawing on Iran’s successful experience in national security-building," Bagheri was quoted as saying by IRNA. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly also confirmed the visit in a post on X, saying that the meetings would be held on Monday. According to him, Minister of Defence Prince Khalid will lead the Saudi delegation during the meeting between Makkah pact countries and Iranian officials. He said the "representatives of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement countries will meet" with Iranian President Pezeshkian and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Rezaei. Krimly described the visit as “part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Defence Alliance members for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis, and promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by Qatar and Pakistan”. "The visit underscores the pivotal role of Makkah Defence Alliance members in reinforcing regional security and stability, and working with all countries in the region to achieve that goal,” he added. In Tehran, Iran’s Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the meeting with officials from the three countries would cover “most pressing issues threatening our region”, which included Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in Palestine and Lebanon. He also said that the topic of “top priority on the agenda would be consequences of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran and its ramifications for the entire region”. The US and Iran signed the Islamabad MoU in June to restore peace in West Asia, advance negotiations on regional security and other contentious issues. The deal ended the conflict that began on February 28 and continued till April 8, when the ceasefire was agreed, followed by talks mediated by Pakistan. Field Marshal Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi have made multiple trips to Tehran as part of Islamabad's efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region. Munir's last visit to Tehran coincided with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's unannounced trip to West Asia. During his meeting with Munir last week, Rezaei told the Pakistani army chief that all enriched nuclear materials will remain in Iran as a national asset, stressing that no negotiations with the US will take place until Washington builds trust by meeting Iran’s conditions, according to the channel. Also, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov last week travelled to Tehran, where he met Iranian leaders and discussed everything from Europe to West Asia, including Lebanon, Palestine, Ukraine and Yemen.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up the Tamil Nadu government for repeatedly seeking adjournments in a matter concerning compensation for property and business losses caused by communal riots of 1996 in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin), questioning its failure to ensure timely relief to the victims.

However, the State government subsequently issued Government Order G.O.Ms.No.1834, granting uniform compensation of Rs.
2 lakh to all affected persons.
The decision was challenged before the Madras High Court.
Both the Single Judge and the Division Bench favoured compensation in accordance with the recommendations of the one-man commission.
The State government subsequently challenged the High Court's decisions before the Supreme Court.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) response to a plea alleging large-scale deletion of voters from Maharashtra’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, while declining to immediately extend the deadline for filing claims and objections.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the ECI on a petition filed by Arun Anandagiri, who alleged that 33% of voters had been deleted from the state’s electoral rolls during the SIR exercise.

He told the court that around 3,500 redevelopment projects were underway in Mumbai and Pune, with old housing societies being demolished and thousands of residents being relocated.

According to the petitioner, such displacement could put voters at risk of losing their names from the electoral rolls if their current address or other details could not be matched during the revision process.
Datar also questioned the use of Form 6 for voters who were already enrolled in previous elections.
He argued that Form 6 is meant for registering new voters and that existing voters should not be required to use the same form to retain their names on the electoral rolls.
The petitioner sought a separate form or process for voters whose names had already appeared on earlier electoral rolls.

stories.title: Supreme Court Permits Ashish Mishra To Visit Lakhimpur Kheri For Diwali

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday heard the bail-related proceedings of Ashish Mishra, son of former Union Minister Ajay Mishra Teni, in the Lakhimpur Kheri violence case and allowed him permission to visit his hometown to celebrate Diwali with his family and close relatives till November 16.

A three-judge bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was seized of the matter arising from the October 3, 2021 incident in which five persons, including four farmers and a journalist, were killed after vehicles allegedly linked to Mishra's convoy ran over protesting farmers in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh.
The farmers were agitating against the now-repealed farm laws.
The Court had earlier granted him bail subject to the condition that he not enter Lakhimpur Kheri except to appear in the trial.
The condition was later relaxed to permit him to visit his hometown on weekends.
Though bail was confirmed, the Court kept the matter pending to monitor the progress of the trial.

During today's hearing, Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for the victims' side, expressed satisfaction with recent development regarding the transfer of the trial judge, on whom they had expressed a lack of confidence.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Ashish Mishra, submitted that the transfer was a routine administrative exercise and not based on any suspicion or adverse finding against the judge.
Chief Justice Surya Kant clarified that the Court was not casting any aspersions on anyone.
“We are not saying anything against anyone.
Whatever correctional measures the High Court has taken, good enough,” the CJI observed.
The Court had earlier directed the Allahabad High Court to take appropriate action on the report of the HC vigilance regarding the trial judge.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks SCBA Not To Declare Result Of November 2 General Body Meeting On Electoral Reforms
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks SCBA Not To Declare Result Of November 2 General Body Meeting On Electoral Reforms
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) to hold its scheduled general body meeting on November 2 to discuss election reforms, but directed that voting must take place by secret ballot and that the outcome must not be declared.
The results are to be placed before the Court in a sealed envelope.

The directions were issued by a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, who heads the Court-appointed committee examining the SCBA reform, made an oral mention and raised concerns over the proposed meeting.

Gupta pointed out that the SCBA had called a special general body meeting to pass two resolutions linked to the Court's May 29 order, one relating to proximity card entry and the other concerning veteran members, ahead of the November 5 hearing in the matter of SCBA v BD Kaushik(in which the Court is monitoring the SCBA electoral reforms).

Gupta submitted that while he was not opposing any resolution, the meeting was being convened without consultation and appeared to overreach the Court's order, especially since the matter is listed for hearing just three days later.
He also cautioned that any resolution passed would become binding immediately.

SCBA President Senior Advocate Pradeep Rai responded that the association wanted to ascertain the views of its members and that any concerns could have been resolved through discussion rather than approaching the Court.
“Instead of coming to this Court, we could have resolved it.
Why waste the valuable time of this Court?” Rai said, adding that the executive committee preferred consulting members before forming an opinion.
CJI Surya Kant clarified that the court-appointed committee's proposals aim to strengthen genuine practitioners rather than curtail their rights.
“Those who are genuinely regular visitors to the Supreme Court, having an interest in the Bar, the institution and the system, we want to strengthen their hands.
All those outsiders who have nothing to do with the profession should be isolated and excluded,” the Chief Justice observed.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Had 23 Years To Settle Legislative Privilege Vs Free Speech. It Chose Not To
stories.title: Supreme Court Had 23 Years To Settle Legislative Privilege Vs Free Speech. It Chose Not To
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: On October 6, 2026, a seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court disposed of one of the most significant constitutional references of the last two decades.
The question was straightforward: can a state legislature use its privileges under Article 194(3) to punish a journalist for what they write?
The answer, after 23 years: we will not say.
Not today.
Not in this case.
Come back when someone else gets arrested.
The reference arose from the N. Ravi case.
In April 2003, The Hindu published an editorial titled "Rising Intolerance," criticising the government of then Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa.
The Tamil Nadu Assembly responded by passing a breach of privilege resolution.
On November 7, 2003, Speaker K. Kalimuthu found the editorial constituted a breach.
Police arrested five Hindu staff members within hours.
The Supreme Court stayed the arrests three days later, but the constitutional question of what happens when Article 194(3) collides with Article 19(1)(a) remained unresolved.

An internal probe into alleged disclosure of confidential information by two senior executives remains active and unresolved.
